did: I drew characters for the essays' speaking bubbles. First I put options on a private page: a barn owl, the mochi from the brand mark and a fox for you, and porcelain heads or tin birds for Kokoro's voices. You chose the mochi and the tin birds, and kept the owl for later. They are now in the one shared bubble that the Rust Rounds essay, the interview essay and a cards essay's spoken card all draw. They come in through a new template version (and for spoken cards, through the cheat-sheet series), so essays already published keep the flat icons. The Rust essay's template preview shows them.

calls.title: Which essays get the characters (C822)
options: only new template versions, through a field in the template's shape
always the newest version, for every essay
calls.why: A published essay never redraws differently from what was released. An essay with an opening takes the new version, so home's render image refuses it until you rebuild that image. An essay without an opening keeps the flat icons.
calls.undo: Drop the cast from the Rust essay's version 6 and the interview essay's version 3, and set both producers back to versions 5 and 2.

calls.title: How the characters will move (C821)
options: SVG and CSS in a HyperFrames composition, drawn from the same character data
calls.why: HyperFrames is already pinned, CI already proves its renders are the same bytes twice, and it costs nothing. Rive would add a second renderer that proof doesn't cover yet, plus a hosted editor account. Lottie needs After Effects or a freemium editor, and the mouth moving per word would be our own code anyway.
calls.undo: Choose Rive or Lottie when step 2 starts. The characters are data, so either can redraw them.

left: Step 2, the motion, waits on your next look at the still characters. While speaking: the mouth moves per word, a gentle jiggle, and the tin bird's key turns. At rest: a blink and a breath. It counts as done when the Rust essay's template preview shows the motion.
Home's render image needs rebuilding from a some-ui with #3322 before the next essay with an opening renders.
Tear, point, look and move stay for later, as further cases of the same expression set.
